title: Plan Administration Rule: Expiry, Renewal and Retention on a Protection Plan
content:
Coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans that runs to a fixed term expires on its expiry date, and coverage written as lifetime runs for as long as the customer owns the piece and never expires of itself. Coverage that may be renewed is renewed only inside the renewal window before expiry, and the renewed premium carries the coverage's uplift. A plan is expired, and its closing date recorded, only while it stands at active, inspection overdue, suspended or exhausted. A plan whose allowance has been consumed is recorded as exhausted rather than expired, and it still expires on its own expiry date when the term runs out. Once a plan has expired it answers for nothing, including a loss that happened before expiry but was reported after it, and the customer is directed to fresh coverage where the piece still qualifies. Claim documentation is retained for the years the coverage sets, counted from the date of the settlement or the refusal.

## Standings from which a plan is expired

| Standing of the plan | Its expiry and closing date are recorded from here |
|---|---|
| active | yes |
| inspection overdue | yes |
| suspended | yes |
| exhausted | yes |
| quoted, cancelled, transferred | no |

The standing is read from the plan record before the expiry is recorded.

## Points of judgement

**A plan whose allowance was consumed six months ago.** It is recorded as exhausted rather than expired, and it still expires on its own expiry date when the term runs out.

**A loss that happened in the last week of the term but was reported a month after expiry.** The plan answers for nothing once it has expired, and that includes a loss that happened before expiry but was reported after it. Where the piece still qualifies, the customer is directed to fresh coverage.

**Lifetime coverage and expiry.** Coverage written as lifetime runs for as long as the customer owns the piece and never expires of itself, so no expiry date falls due on it.
